transcript:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (Orion Head of ML), Tom Bennett (Orion CTO), Priya Nair (Product), Alex Gomez (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick review of POC success criteria, agreed go/no-go thresholds for latency/cost/quality, and acceptance test reporting format; owner/responsibilities assigned.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros, and then we'll jump to the success criteria doc we shared.
[00:08] Sara Lopez: Hey Maya, hi Liam. thanks, we've looked through the deck. main thing for us is we need confidence on latency at 95th pct for our peak traffic, and that model outputs don't regress on our fraud detection labels.
[00:20] Liam Park: yup, totally — we'll propose an acceptance test that covers both. propose to run two benchmark slices: steady-state peak QPS and tail-latency spikes.
[00:31] Tom Bennett: want to confirm, are you recommending Dedicated or hosted for the POC? we have compliance concerns so private is an option but longer lead time.
[00:40] Maya Chen: good question. For speed of setup and to get benchmark numbers fast, Dedicated reserved test pool is best; we can also run a VPC-hosted private variant later if you need KMS/HSM. for the acceptance tests we will run both Dedicated and a hosted fallback so you can compare unit costs.
[00:56] Priya Nair: timeline — we talked 6 weeks earlier. can you propose milestones?
[01:03] Liam Park: yeah, milestone 1 (week 1): environment and sample data ingestion. milestone 2 (week 2-3): run benchmarks, iterate quantization and batching config. milestone 3 (week 4): integrate into your canary route and run traffic replay. week 5-6: soak and measure acceptance metrics, produce final report.
[01:21] Sara Lopez: ok sounds reasonable. for success criteria we want clear go/no-go thresholds: 95th pct latency <= 220ms for short prompt (our common path), mean token cost < $0.0009 per token equivalent, and detection F1 not drop more than 1.5% vs baseline.
[01:40] Liam Park: got it. We'll encode that as: 95p latency under 220ms at target QPS, 99p tail within 500ms when under load, and quality metric as F1 delta <= 1.5%. We'll also report percent of requests served from prefix cache to show cost improvement.
[01:58] Alex Gomez: about sample traffic — we can provide 24 hours of production-like traces, anonymized. is that enough?
[02:05] Maya Chen: yes, that will let us do sequence-length distributions and sizing. If you can also share typical concurrency and peak QPS windows that helps tuning batch sizes and KV cache heuristics.
[02:18] Tom Bennett: security question: audit logs and SSO. we need SSO + RBAC and access logs for the Dedicated pool. any limits there?
[02:26] Liam Park: Dedicated supports SAML SSO and role-based policies. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM; we have integrations with Splunk/Datadog. For Private on-prem we can integrate with your existing KMS/HSM.
[02:40] Priya Nair: reporting format — can you put the final acceptance report as a simple spreadsheet + short write-up? product wants clear pass/fail per acceptance criterion.
[02:49] Maya Chen: yes we'll produce a spreadsheet with per-test rows: test name, target metric, observed metric, pass/fail, notes. We'll also include plots for latency distributions and token cost breakdown by route.
[03:03] Sara Lopez: on the quality side, how will you measure F1? do you run our labels against outputs or do you need additional instrumentation?
[03:10] Liam Park: we'll run your labeled dataset as an offline eval and then replay a sample of production traffic through the POC endpoint to measure online deltas. both offline and online measures will be included.
[03:20] Maya Chen: quick note about benchmarks: we'll run three configurations — baseline (your current service), Redwood Dedicated with recommended quantization, and Redwood hosted fallback without quantization to measure tradeoffs.
[03:33] Tom Bennett: if Dedicated shows >2x cost reduction but F1 drops 2%, that would be a tough tradeoff. our go/no-go says F1 delta must be <=1.5% or else it's fail. correct?
[03:45] Sara Lopez: yes, that's our stick. cost matters but not at expense of material model degradation.
[03:51] Maya Chen: understood — we'll make that explicit in the acceptance table.
[04:00] [05:12] Liam Park: small transcription hiccup here — when we run the benchmark, we'll capture per-token cost, prefix cache hit, and batching efficiency. We'll also provide recommended knob settings — batch size, KV cache TTL, and quantization profile.
[05:28] Alex Gomez: about the environment — we prefer a test VPC with a limited subnet and IAM roles, we'll give you temporary access. Alex: i'll provision the test subnet by 8/14.
[05:40] Priya Nair: who signs off? product (Priya) + ML (Sara) + infra (Alex)?
[05:47] Sara Lopez: yes, sign-off requires all three. sign-off rubric is per criterion pass.
[05:52] Maya Chen: we'll include a sign-off page in the report with checkboxes for each owner.
[06:00] [10:12] Sara Lopez: one practical question — do you support function calling / structured outputs? our pipeline expects JSON with fields for scores and flags.
[10:21] Liam Park: yes, runtime supports structured output. we'll include examples and show how to map into your downstream pipeline.
[10:30] Tom Bennett: about timelines again, if things go well can we have a shortened POC that focuses only on the online replay and a small acceptance set?
[10:39] Maya Chen: we can — that's essentially a 3-week focused POC, but full confidence needs the soak week. we can propose a fast-track option in the SOW.
[10:48] Priya Nair: cost of the POC itself? we expect Redwood to cover engineering time?
[10:53] Maya Chen: standard POC pricing is a modest credit plus cost of Dedicated infra during benchmarking. we'll send a transparent breakdown in the pricing doc.
[11:04] [20:00] Liam Park: ok let's concretely capture acceptance tests — listing now:
 - Test A: 95p latency test on short prompt (50 tokens) at target QPS (we'll use your peak window) — threshold: <= 220ms
 - Test B: tail latency resilience with burst traffic — 99p <= 500ms
 - Test C: Quality eval using labeled dataset — F1 delta <= 1.5%
 - Test D: Cost measurement — mean token-equivalent cost < $0.0009 (or 20% improvement vs baseline)
 - Test E: Reliability — error rate < 0.1% over 24-hour soak

[20:35] Sara Lopez: looks good. please add pass/fail logic and how you compute token-equivalent cost (includes batching amortization and cache hits).
[20:42] Liam Park: yes, we'll include formulas in appendix. token-equivalent cost = total infra cost / effective tokens served after cache/batch discounts.
[20:51] Alex Gomez: we will want the raw benchmark logs for our audit. can you provide them?
[20:56] Maya Chen: yes, raw logs and latency histograms will be shared. we'll scrub any sensitive PII; you can also request the logs to be delivered to your S3 bucket.
[21:08] Priya Nair: acceptance report format: spreadsheet + short doc + recorded benchmarks. can we get a template?
[21:14] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll attach a template with the SOW.
[21:21] [30:10] Tom Bennett: outstanding dependencies to start: access to anonymized traces, SSO/RBAC requirements doc, and confirmation of budget for Dedicated infra during the benchmark.
[30:28] Sara Lopez: i'll push for the budget today.
[30:35] Maya Chen: great. last thing — can we walk through example pass/fail scenario? say Dedicated meets latency and cost, but F1 delta is 1.8%. That's a fail by your rubric?
[30:47] Sara Lopez: yes, fail — we'd at that point either tune quantization, fallback to hosted variant for important routes, or ask for custom fine-tuning.
[30:56] Liam Park: we can attempt quantization adjustments and different kernel selections to recover quality; we'll also provide a recommended fallback routing policy per route.
[31:10] [40:00] Priya Nair: ok, everything here seems actionable. let's confirm owners on the sheet: Maya send pricing/security and report template; Liam prepare benchmark scripts and quant profiles; Sara provide traces and labels; Alex set up VPC.
[40:25] Maya Chen: confirmed — i'll also schedule the benchmark week in your calendar for 8/18.
[40:33] Alex Gomez: i'll have the VPC ready by 8/14 as noted.
[40:40] Sara Lopez: we'll have labels and 24h traces shared by 8/11.
[40:46] Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[40:50] Tom Bennett: none from me. thanks.
[40:53] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the SOW, pricing, security pack, and the template.
[41:00] Sara Lopez: thanks.

[End of call]
